$comment: Repo registry (policy, no secrets): which repos the factory manages and what it is allowed to do in each. Runtime config stays in factory/config/<owner>_<repo>.json; the per-deployment supervision file with webhook secrets lives in fleet/. Four decisions are policy because their failure mode is not a crash: whether a repo may be auto-merged (autoMerge), which label makes an issue eligible for pickup (eligibilityLabel), which paths a run may change (pathAllowlist; vendor/ is protected everywhere regardless), and whether a passing test run is required before a branch may be pushed (requireVerification, default true — see research/multi-repo-factory-plan.md §5.19). Safety flags must be real booleans: Boolean("false") is true, so strings are rejected at load. See research/multi-repo-factory-plan.md §5.11.

repos.note: N3 dogfood target, ENABLED and PUBLISHED (fleet entry plus a public HTTPS front per fleet/enable-self-work.md). Nothing starts a run by itself: an eligible event from an allowlisted sender is required - the `build` label on an issue, or a `/factory` comment on an open factory PR. Runs are also started deliberately against this checkout via gates/self-run-task.mjs. autoMerge is false permanently — drydock runs stop at the draft PR for a human to merge (§5.11). pathAllowlist deliberately excludes gates/ so a self-run cannot edit the oracles that judge it, and gates/probes/ is additionally protected. README.md and AGENTS.md are writable by decision E1 (2026-10-31): self-work documents itself, including its own operating rules, because the file is advisory while the enforcement points live outside the workspace — this registry and the reviewer. An AGENTS.md edit only changes future behaviour once a human merges it. prFeedback is enabled (#67): when a listener is published per fleet/enable-self-work.md, a "/factory …" comment from an allowlisted sender on an OPEN pull request reworks that PR — restricted by host-side checks to the factory's own agent/issue-<n> branches, never a human branch, and it still ends at a draft push with verification and review intact. refine is enabled (#65): the `refine` label on an issue, or a `/refine <guidance>` comment on an issue, runs a read-only expansion pass (`read` tool only, remote scrubbed) whose sole output is a comment on that issue — it starts no work and grants nothing, because acting still requires the `build` label plus path scope, verification and review. Issue #99 (six cycles spent on an impossible ticket) is the cost this step exists to avoid.

Kernel repo managed by the factory. testCommand uses test:unit (pure-logic subset) because the sealed sandbox has network=none and the full suite needs a live model endpoint — see engram#66. poc/lib/ is protected because drydock vendors it and a factory run must not break the pin discipline. autoMerge false: stops at draft PR for human merge.
